output.summary: KEP-5975 proposes that API directories contain only the code that differs from the standard pattern, with a trivial storage registration (registry.NewREST with a RESTConfig) and generated or default wiring for codegen, validation, field wiping, generation management, and feature-gated field dropping. Status is provisional (stage stable).
output.rationale: Every strategy file in pkg/registry/ reimplements the same ~12 methods across 67 files (~12,000 lines), and this has caused costly mistakes. The KEP builds on declarative validation (KEP-4153, KEP-5073) and declarative defaulting (KEP-1929) to drive standard behavior from types.go tags. It keeps backward compatibility: external users must opt in to the new behaviors.

alternatives.option: Declarative tags for all strategy behavior
alternatives.why_not: Tags break down for complex validation options, cross-field generation tracking, custom warnings, and injected dependencies; the KEP keeps strategy and storage definitions in Go for type safety.

alternatives.option: Enabling generators via a per-directory apigroup.yaml-style config file
alternatives.why_not: Not chosen as the KEP text; the author removed references to YAML files after review feedback. Discussion treated it as a separate, related change (kubernetes PR 138657).

alternatives.option: Merging the narrower enforcement change in kubernetes PR 138577
alternatives.why_not: Mentioned by the author as the alternative to this broader change, which would consume more review bandwidth; the sources do not state why it was not taken.
Raised by the author as an alternative to the current generic wiping approach; the sources do not record a decision on it.

evidence.quote: Every strategy file in `pkg/registry/` implements the same ~12 methods: status clearing, generation bumping, validation delegation, and feature-gate field dropping.
All changes will be backwards compatible. External users of API frameworks and code generators will need to opt-in to the new behaviors.
These behaviors should be driven by information already available in the API definition (types.go files) such as declarative validation and feature gate tags.
Existing generator usage is unchanged. All flags/args/tags will continue to be supported.
I've removed the reference to yaml files and responded to all feedback.
